git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of the eleven rules in the case's list, so all eleven are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/library-client-skill.json and no verdict rests on a changed sentence. The diff touches "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (both on `for`), macros.md (edited examples and one new rule) and one example in processes.md. None of the five files contains a `for`, a macro or `:ets`, so the changes reach no line here.

Result against the previous sweep: 0 of 5 runs violate any listed rule. The only tier cell that changes is Make polymorphism explicit on Haiku, violated in 2026-10-31 and clean here. haiku-1 and haiku-2 both route the key, base URL and timeout through a guarded check_options!/1; the sentence applied is the unchanged "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument" (idiomatic-elixir/references/library-design.md line 60). Its second clause raises ArgumentError rather than failing with a FunctionClauseError, but the error is raised in WeatherClient, before Req, which the case's check asks for, so both are clean. haiku-1 was run against the stub on a copy reordered to compile; the other four as written. All five raise inside WeatherClient for a charlist key, a bad base_url and a bad timeout (and a non-list req_options where the option exists). haiku-1 and haiku-2 accept an empty key; the rule asks for a type check, so this is not counted.

In multi-clause functions: these are the functions of three or more clauses. opus-1 Error.message/1 (lines 44, 48, 52, 56) selects by literals and takes the struct whole. haiku-1 handle_response/1 (lines 89, 93, 97, 101) binds body in two clauses, status in three (a literal in the first, guard-read in the second) and exception in the fourth. sonnet-1 parse_response/1 (lines 173, 177, 182) and sonnet-2 handle_response/1 (lines 181, 186, 190) bind status and body in two clauses and exception in the third. haiku-2 has none. In no function is one body-only field bound in every clause, so 0 of 5 violated. Spread heads: opus-1 parse_forecast/1 (lines 232-236), haiku-2 parse_forecast/1 (lines 129-133) and sonnet-1 Forecast.from_body/1 (lines 37-41) spread, and check_options!/1 in haiku-1 (line 69) and haiku-2 (line 102) spreads once mix format runs; each binds only keys its guard reads, which the rule allows. sonnet-2's transcript shows its first validate_options/1 head spread under mix format, and it rewrote the head to `%__MODULE__{} = client` with `client.base_url` and the like in the guard (lines 175-177).

Use exception structs and Return: haiku-1 (line 101) and haiku-2 (through the with at line 96) return Req's own exception for a failed request. These are defexception structs, and evals/sweeps/2026-10-22/grades/library-client-skill.json and evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/library-client-baseline.json graded that shape clean, so it is clean here. The private check_options!/1 in both raises for invalid options and has no non-bang version; it is graded clean under Return, as the previous sweep graded sonnet-2's private base_url!/1, since library-design.md allows raising for invalid arguments.

Not counted, but noted. In sonnet-1, build/4 takes the API key as an argument, so a bad base_url, timeout or req_options raises a FunctionClauseError whose printed arguments include the key: against the stub it printed WeatherClient.build("SECRETKEY", 1, 10000, []). Keep secrets out of logs and inspect output names only struct Inspect output, so this is not counted, as in the previous sweep. The other four do not show the key this way: opus-1 passes one value to each validate_* function, haiku-1 and haiku-2 raise a message without it, and sonnet-2's validate_options/1 takes the struct, whose Inspect hides it. haiku-2's @doc (line 70) says a missing :api_key raises KeyError; against the stub, struct!/2 raises ArgumentError, because the key is in @enforce_keys. No rule covers this.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the previous grades. with rule: haiku-2's with (lines 96-99) has two steps. do: rule: haiku-1 handle_response/1, haiku-2 parse_response/1 and opus-1 parse_forecast/1 mix a do: clause with block clauses, which the rule allows and the previous sweep did not count. Naming: haiku-1's and haiku-2's private get_forecast/3 and sonnet-2's public fetch_forecast/3 name HTTP requests, not key lookups, and are not counted. Match every expected shape: nobody sends a status its documents exclude; opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 document their API error as any non-2xx status, haiku-1 labels the rest "unexpected HTTP status", and haiku-2's Error moduledoc names no status range. Build a multi-line argument: "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 476) would apply to struct literals written over several lines that fit in 98 characters: opus-1 lines 238-242 and sonnet-1 lines 43-47 and 155-160. The previous sweep left the same shape unflagged (haiku-2 line 115, sonnet-2 line 164), so these are not counted, to keep the sweeps comparable. A grader reading the sentence strictly would flag them.
